title: The order form
scenario:
Your studio makes images for a coffee brand's autumn launch. You use the OpenAI image settings from this lesson. Three jobs are in the exhibit. The client call is on Thursday.

The exhibit is our own job sheet, not a vendor format. The log lines are made up for this case.
exhibit:
Job sheet
  Job 1  A poster print that needs 4K, from a Gemini 3 image model that supports 4K.
  Job 2  One hero banner. The client will ask for changes live on a call.
  Job 3  A cup logo sticker, 1024x1024, with NO background.

Log from an earlier test (made up for this case)
  typed prompt:   Autumn latte on a wooden table, soft light
  revised_prompt: A latte in a ceramic mug on a wooden table next to a
                  cinnamon stick, soft warm light, shallow depth of field

Another test, on a Gemini image model
  asked for: 8 images        files received: 7

questions.prompt: Which approach fits job 2, the hero banner changed live on a call?

options.text: Set quality to max on every request so the first try is perfect and no changes are needed.
options.explanation: OpenAI says to use low quality for quick drafts and compare higher settings for finals. A max setting does not remove the need to iterate.

options.text: Ten new one-shot requests, one for each comment from the client, each with the full prompt retyped.
options.explanation: One-shot is for a single image from one prompt. For iterating, both vendors point to a conversation.

options.text: A conversation: the Responses API or a Gemini multi-turn chat, each change a follow-up.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI points to the Responses API for conversational, editable image work. Google calls multi-turn conversation the recommended way to iterate on images.

options.text: Set n to 20 and let the client pick the best of 20.
options.explanation: n asks for more images from the same prompt. It does not apply the client's comments to an image.

questions.prompt: A print needs 4K from a Gemini 3 image model that supports 4K. What do you set?

options.text: image_size set to 2K, which is the highest size Gemini 3 allows
options.explanation: 2K is above the default but below the 4K the print needs. 4K is also allowed, so 2K is not the highest size.

options.text: image_size set to 4k, with a lowercase k
options.explanation: Google says lowercase values such as 1k will be rejected. The K must be uppercase.

options.text: image_size set to 4K, with an uppercase K
options.explanation: Right. Google says Gemini 3 image models make 1K by default, and 2K or 4K must be requested. The K must be uppercase.

options.text: Leave image_size unset and ask for "print quality" in the prompt
options.explanation: Unset means the default, which is 1K. A print that needs 4K would be too small.

questions.prompt: Which settings fit job 3, the logo sticker with no background?

options.text: background transparent, with png as the file type
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's rule: set background to transparent and use png or webp.

options.text: background opaque, then cut the cup out by hand in a design tool
options.explanation: This can work, but the guide gives a direct setting for it. Hand work adds time and risk for no gain.

options.text: background auto, with png as the file type
options.explanation: auto lets the model decide from the prompt. It does not guarantee a transparent background.

options.text: background transparent, with jpeg as the file type
options.explanation: The guide pairs transparent backgrounds with png or webp. jpeg is not on that list.

questions.prompt: The client asks why the test image shows a cinnamon stick that nobody typed. Where do you look first?

options.text: The file type of the saved image, such as png or webp
options.explanation: The file type decides how the image is stored. It does not add objects.

options.text: The n setting, the number of images made per request
options.explanation: n sets how many images one request makes. It does not change the prompt text.

options.text: The revised_prompt field of the call, next to the image
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says the mainline model revises your prompt in the image generation tool, and the revised text comes back in revised_prompt. The log shows the cinnamon stick there.

options.text: The size setting, the shape and pixel size of the image
options.explanation: Size sets the shape and resolution of the image. It does not add objects.

questions.prompt: On the Gemini test, 8 images were requested and 7 came back. How should you read this?

options.text: The request was invalid, so it must be reported to the vendor and sent again later.
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs says a short count is an invalid request. Google lists it as a known limit.

options.text: The last image was lost because the quality setting was too low for the job.
options.explanation: The Gemini guide lists no quality setting, and a missing image is not linked to quality anywhere in it.

options.text: The model does not always follow the exact count, so count the files and plan for it.
options.explanation: Right. Google's limits list says the model "won't always follow the exact number of image outputs" you ask for.

options.text: The client's account has a daily limit of 7 images, so the eighth was cut.
options.explanation: Nothing in the exhibit or the guide points to a limit of 7. The docs describe the count as not guaranteed.
